sources.searcher_note: NADAC table row: the solution sits at $0.4735/mL in July 2026 (also $0.4741 June, $0.4741 May), close to the lead's 2024 end price of $0.434/mL, so the high level persisted. Shows only 2026 rows (older history paywalled); does not report the 2024 jump itself. Date is the NADAC row date.

Saxagliptin 2.5 mg NADAC $1.127 per tablet in July 2026, back near the lead's pre-jump $1.35 (lead is 5 mg, 2024). Different strength and window; suggests the 2024 rise did not last. No 5 mg rows or 2024 history visible.

sources.outlet: The Ohio State University College of Pharmacy
sources.quote: For the first time, a large chain pharmacy participated in the NADAC survey and reported invoice prices across all locations selected.
sources.searcher_note: Caveat for any 2024 NADAC step: rates swung in 2024 because chain pharmacies entered and left the survey (again in November 2024), so some big week-to-week moves are survey-mix artifacts, not real market prices. No drugs named.

notes: No news, trade press or government source found naming a 2024 price jump for acetaminophen-codeine oral solution or saxagliptin, or counting 3x+ NADAC steps in 2024. 46brooklyn's 2024 monthly and year-in-review reports were scanned (page text) and mention neither drug. No 2024 shortage or discontinuation notice found for acetaminophen-codeine oral solution (ASHP results were for promethazine-codeine and hydrocodone-APAP) or for saxagliptin (generics approved 2023; brand Onglyza discontinued per GoodRx snippet). Current price-guide pages (Drugs.com: oral liquid from $10.35 per 473 mL with coupon; rxfinder: saxagliptin average NADAC $1.09, page dated 2026-09-25) are cash/coupon or later-window figures, not recorded as sources. CMS changed generic NADAC to a three-month moving average from December 2024 (per medicaid.gov snippet), which also affects week-level comparisons.
